sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of HIT and the aHIT Variant
sections.description: This section provides the foundational medical knowledge required to understand the case, focusing on the mechanisms of classic Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) and the distinct characteristics of the autoimmune variant (aHIT).
subtopics: The role of Unfractionated Heparin (UFH) and Platelet Factor 4 (PF4)
Classic HIT: Mechanism of IgG-mediated platelet activation via Fc receptor clustering
Autoimmune HIT (aHIT): Heparin-independent platelet activation
Clinical spectrum and severity: Comparing classic HIT with the aHIT phenotype
The paradox of HIT: Thrombocytopenia accompanied by a prothrombotic state

sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Early Diagnostic Workup
sections.description: This section analyzes the patient's presentation, focusing on the timeline of thrombocytopenia and the initial clinical indicators that suggested HIT over other postoperative complications.
subtopics: Post-cardiac surgery thrombocytopenia: Common vs. rare etiologies
The 'Temporal Window' of HIT: Typical onset vs. early onset due to preoperative heparin exposure
Recognizing systemic complications: Analyzing the left parietal stroke as a thrombotic event
Initial laboratory screening: Interpreting the PF4/polyanion ELISA
Differential diagnosis of severe postoperative thrombocytopenia (e.g., TTP, drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia)

sections.section_title: Advanced Diagnostics: The Serotonin Release Assay (SRA)
sections.description: This section explains the gold-standard diagnostic test used in this case, detailing how clinicians interpreted the atypical results to confirm a diagnosis of aHIT.
subtopics: Principles of the Serotonin Release Assay (SRA) as a functional test
Interpreting SRA profiles: Heparin-dependent vs. heparin-independent activation
The role of Fc receptor-blocking monoclonal antibodies (IV.3) in HIT diagnosis
Analyzing 'Indeterminate' results: Partial resistance to Fc receptor blockade
The significance of the patient's unique serological profile in severe aHIT

sections.description: This section covers the therapeutic decisions made to manage the patient's severe thrombocytopenia and high thrombotic risk, including the transition between different anticoagulants.
subtopics: Alternative anticoagulation in HIT: Direct Thrombin Inhibitors (Argatroban) vs. Factor Xa Inhibitors (Fondaparinux)
Treatment of the autoimmune component: High-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) and its expected response
Monitoring for HIT-associated consumptive coagulopathy: Fibrinogen, D-dimer, and schistocyte analysis
The importance of Antithrombin (AT) levels when initiating fondaparinux
Balancing the risk of bleeding (recent stroke) with the risk of thrombosis in severe HIT

sections.description: The final section summarizes the clinical course and highlights the key pedagogical takeaways regarding the diagnosis and management of atypical HIT.
subtopics: Synthesis of the patient's recovery trajectory and neurological outcome
The critical importance of detailed patient history (identifying preoperative heparin exposure)
Identifying red flags for severe aHIT: Deep nadirs and refractory thrombocytopenia
Understanding the evolution of HIT antibodies over time (the transition from aHIT back to typical HIT)
Summary of the novel insights provided by this case for future clinical practice
